A rundown of the Helio testing activities over the last month. 
ZURB  |  March 5th, 2026

Does the new homepage & platform 
page design outperform the old 
versions?
UX Metrics
● Comprehension
● Sentiment  
Audiences 
● Technical leader (US, UK, GR & FR)
● AI Infrastructure and Technical Leaders (Global)
● Infrastructure Owner (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Front-end & Full Stack Developers (Global)
● Non-Technical Leaders (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Financial Decision Makers (US)
Rebrand: Homepage
Concept 176

The homepage and platform pages 
outperform the old designs.
Assumption
● New color scheme feels less abrasive than past 
orange-heavy designs
● Better spacing lets the page breath.
Rebrand Redesigns 
Hunch Concept 176

Experiment with new hero copy on the 
homepage:
Low impressions of conversational and friendly 
bring down the overall sentiment, mostly due to 
the messaging on the page.
Rebrand Redesigns
Recommendation
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework

The homepage redesign is 
polarizing for visitors who 
understand the oﬀer but don’t 
feel the messaging is friendly 
or conversational. 
Sentiment of the newly designed 
homepage dropped from about 50% 
to 33%, despite similar 
comprehension scores as the 
previous version.
Rebrand Redesigns
Signal
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Removing the pop-ups and 
banners from the new 
homepage increases positive 
sentiment. 
Sentiment increased on the current 
version of the homepage from 33% 
to 43% when removing some of the 
busy components at the top of the 
page.
Rebrand Redesigns
Signal
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Rebrand Redesigns
Decisions
Implement
Reﬁne Design
Test Iteration
Revisit Later
Do Not Pursue

Change hero copy.
-> Easy to test, diﬃcult to implement

page design outperform the old

● Financial Decision Makers (US)
Rebrand: Platform Page
Concept 176

The homepage and platform pages 
outperform the old designs.
Assumption
● New color scheme feels less abrasive than past 
orange-heavy designs
● Better spacing lets the page breath.
● The infographic may be too overwhelming
Rebrand Redesigns 
Hunch Concept 176

Iterate on hero copy to clarify product 
oﬀering:
Low sentiment stems from the lack of clarity in 
messaging about the product.
Simplify infographic to present no more 
than 12 items for users to understand:
From our previous infographic testing, we know 
that graphics with more layers to understand test 
poorly. The much simpler graphic on the 
rebranded EDC page received very positive 
reactions.
Rebrand Redesigns
Recommendation
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Low sentiment towards the 
new platform page stems 
from the content feeling 
overly technical and too much 
content competing for 
attention. 
Sentiment of the newly designed 
platform page dropped from about 
53% to 32%, despite similar 
comprehension scores as the 
previous version. Users explained 
that they don’t know where they 
should direct their attention ﬁrst, 
they feel the language is too 
technical/advanced, and there are 
too many diﬀerent content modules.
Rebrand Redesigns
Signal
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework
“the language used can be 
slightly complicated to digest if 
you don't know about large data 
management. Terms I was 
unfamiliar with were things like 
"copy creep" and 
"mission-critical workloads"”
“site appears capable and 
advanced, oﬀering strong 
enterprises solutions, but the 
technical language and features 
makes it somewhat complex to 
understand.”
“Plenty of information but very 
chaotic.”
“Some of these content blocks 
could just be referenced instead 
of full builds… Not everything can 
take the spotlight and this 
company needs to recognize 
when to make the real estate 
trade-oﬀs.”

Engagement with the 
infographic is low on ﬁrst click 
and when looking for a 
speciﬁc layer information. 
Only 2% of participants used their 
ﬁrst click on the infographic, and 
10% of participants were able to ﬁnd 
a piece of information in the layers 
of the graphic.
Rebrand Redesigns
Signal
 Concept 176
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Comprehension of the 
platform page infographic is 
reduced by impressions that it 
is for advanced technical 
leads to understand. 
The infographics comprehension 
score was barely out of the average 
range at 70%, with up to 40% of 
participants indicating they 
understood little to none of what it 
means.
Rebrand Redesigns
Signal
 Concept 176
Source: Helio Survey

Users have trouble seeing 
how the information connects 
in the infographic after 
selecting a layer. 
Sentiment for the infographic is 
poor, with spikes above 10% in 
negative impressions of 
complicated, confusing, and 
overwhelming.

Decisions
Implement

Does the new Evergreen page design 
outperform the old versions?
UX Metrics
● Comprehension
● Appeal
● Sentiment  
Audiences 
● Technical leader (US, UK, GR & FR)
● AI Infrastructure and Technical Leaders (Global)
● Infrastructure Owner (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Front-end & Full Stack Developers (Global)
● Non-Technical Leaders (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Financial Decision Makers (US)
Evergreen Redesign
Concept 178

The Evergreen page may beneﬁt from a 
dark mode approach.
Assumption
● The current redesign mixes dark & light color 
schemes
● The infographic at the top of the current page may 
be confusing to users.
Evergreen Redesign 
Hunch Concept 178

Move forward with new dark mode 
design:
The dark mode signiﬁcantly increased all UX 
metrics tested on the Evergreen page.
Move ROI CTA down page:
Users need more clarity on what is being oﬀered 
before they want to learn about the ROI that it can 
produce.
Evergreen Redesign
Recommendation
 Concept 178
Source: Data Comparison Framework

The dark mode of the 
Evergreen page increases 
appeal towards the page 
while decreasing negative 
impressions of being stiﬀ and 
uncertain. 
UX metrics across the board 
increased for the new variation of 
the Evergreen page, especially in 
terms of sentiment and appeal.
Evergreen Redesign
Signal
 Concept 178
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Visitors aren't interested in 
ROI promises before they 
understand the platform 
oﬀering. 
See Y our ROI Impact was rated one 
of the least helpful pieces of the 
new Evergreen page despite it's 
prominent placement in the hero. 
The 'discover' CTA in the current 
hero is a more interesting CTA for 
visitors.
Evergreen Redesign
Signal
 Concept 178
Source: Data Comparison Framework

SLAs content on the current 
Evergreen page is one of the 
most helpful pieces of 
content. 
Behind the video and how it works 
content, this SLAs section was voted 
as most helpful by a signiﬁcant 
amount of participants reacting to 
the current iteration of the page.
Evergreen Redesign
Signal
 Concept 178
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Increasing infographic 
content at the top of the page 
reduces comprehension and 
sentiment. 
Both versions 2 and 3 of the dark 
mode saw a decrease in 
comprehension and a signiﬁcant 
drop in positive impressions 
towards the page.
Evergreen Redesign
Signal
 Concept 178
Source: Data Comparison Framework

Providing a color-break after 
the hero increases appeal and 
sentiment of the Evergreen 
page. 
We saw the highest sentiment score 
and lowest amount of negative 
impressions when changing the 
second modules background color 
from black to gray.

Everpure Executive Brief (July)
A rundown of the testing activities over the last month with Helio. 
ZURB  |  May 7th, 2026

Everpure wants its Y ouTube channel to work as a 
trusted place where enterprise IT people learn and 
make decisions, not just a brand channel. This test 
established a baseline for how the channel page 
reads to people today, before we benchmark it 
against competitors.
UX Metrics
● Success
● Satisfaction
Audiences 
● Technical leader (US, UK, GR & FR)
● AI Infrastructure and Technical Leaders (Global)
● Infrastructure Owner (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Front-end & Full Stack Developers (Global)
● Non-Technical Leaders (US, UK, GR & FR)
● Financial Decision Makers (US)
YouTube
Concept 198

Solution Page Campaign Mode
Design Concept 197
Source: Helio Test
We tested a single screenshot of 
the current Everpure Y ouTube 
channel home page, from the 
banner down through the 
playlists, Shorts, and videos.

1. The channel reads more like marketing 
than education, because most of the rows 
lead with company programming instead 
of customer problems.
2. People can't easily ﬁnd content organized 
around their challenges, because the 
"Solve Y our Core Challenges" row sits far 
down the page.
3. Viewers struggle to say what Everpure 
actually does after seeing the channel, 
because the same positioning gap keeps 
showing up on the website.
4. People will watch but not subscribe, 
because the page never explains what 
subscribing gets you.
Solution Page Campaign Mode
Hunch Concept 197
Source: Helio Test

● Reorganize the channel home page 
so challenge-based content sits 
above the podcast and series rows.
● Treat the featured video as a 
positioning asset, its job is to

We need to validate whether users understand 
that positioning and whether the 
assessment/workshop ﬂow feels credible, 
useful, and worth engaging with.

EDC Blueprint Page
Concept 191

Whether users understand the EDC Success 
Blueprint positioning and whether the 
assessment/workshop ﬂow feels credible, 
useful, and worth engaging with.
Assumption
● Adding a concrete Blueprint output example 
(a sample roadmap or maturity score 
preview) for enterprise evaluators will 
increase Desirability and Sentiment
● Pushing back "Book a Workshop" relative to 
"Start Y our Assessment" for users arriving 
without prior context will increase 
Completion and reduce Eﬀort.
● Adding a one-line descriptor beneath the 
primary CTA for ﬁrst-time page visitors will 
increase Intent.
EDC Blueprint Page 
Hunch Concept 191
Source: Figma File

Rewrite the hero headline to lead with a 
speciﬁc user outcome, not "Enterprise Data 
Cloud."
Add a CTA descriptor line directly beneath 
"Start Y our Assessment." Copy should name 
the format, the time commitment, and the 
output.  Establish visual hierarchy between 
CTAs. "Start Y our Assessment" should read as 
primary. "Book a Workshop" as secondary.
Insert an audience qualiﬁer in the ﬁrst body 
section. One sentence naming the target role 
and situation. 
Add a Blueprint output preview. A sample 
maturity score, a partial roadmap screenshot, 
or a testimonial that names a speciﬁc output. 
EDC Blueprint Page 
Recommendation Concept 191
Source: Data Comparison

EDC Blueprint Page 
Design Concept 191
Source: Figma File 
EDC Blueprint Baseline
 EDC Page Baseline

A stronger message could 
increase assessment start rates 
by setting a clearer expectation 
for what users will get. 
In the 10-second ﬁrst impression, 
nearly all responses describe the 
page as "data cloud storage," "cloud 
data," or "enterprise data storage." 
Fewer than 5 respondents named the 
Success Blueprint concept, the 
assessment journey, or the three 
outcomes (reduce risk, scale agility, 
increase eﬃciency) without being 
prompted.
EDC Blueprint Page 
Signal Concept 191
Source: Data Comparison

A one-line descriptor beneath 
the CTA, like "Answer 5 
questions. Get a personalized 
EDC roadmap," will align 
expectations before the click.
After clicking on the page, it reveals a 
wide range of expectations, some 
anticipated a business questionnaire, 
others expected a free trial, a signup 
page, or a product test. 
One respondent asked directly: "Why 
would you assume I'd start an 
assessment straight away?"

Signal Concept 191
Source: Data Comparison

The page functions as an 
information hub but not a 
persuasion tool. 
Adding social proof, outcome-speciﬁc 
language, or concrete beneﬁt 
statements (e.g., time savings, risk 
reduction metrics) could shift the 
Neutral block toward Met or 
Exceeded
Emotional response is split between 
"Innovative/Helpful" and 
"Overwhelming/Confusing."

level.
A brief positioning statement that 
names the audience ("If your

This will reduce unqualiﬁed clicks and 
improves lead quality.

but the core keynote/live stream experience 
risks becoming passive and transactional once 
attendees land on the page.

Accelerate Live Stream
Concept 192

Live status is misread as navigation, not 
broadcast.
Assumption
● Visitors need an unmistakable live signal in the 
ﬁrst viewport so they can immediately understand 
that the event is happening now and act on it.
● Visitors arriving during the live window need a 
single dominant action so they can move from 
landing to watching without evaluating competing 
options.
● Adding a single declarative context line, "Pure 
Storage's ﬂagship annual conference · Live now" 
— above the hero for visitors without prior brand 
familiarity will improve ﬁrst-impression 
comprehension
Accelerate Live Stream
Hunch Concept 192
Source: Figma File

Fix live-state legibility before 
anything else. Add a one-line context 
statement at the top of the page
Establish a single dominant CTA 
during the live window. Agenda, 
speakers, venue, and registration 
should be accessible but visually 
subordinate when the keynote is live
Introduce explicit video aﬀordance 
cues. Autoplay creates expectation 
mismatch for a meaningful segment.
The page's visual and editorial 
register… Innovative, Helpful, Exciting,  
is landing correctly.
Build the page to shift states.
Design separate live, pre-event, and 
post-event states.

Recommendation Concept 192
Source: Data Comparison

Accelerate Live Stream
Design Concept 192
Source: Figma File 
Baseline
The page needs to operate 
across three distinct temporal 
states, pre-event (registration 
drive), live event (viewership), 
and post-event (replay + 
follow-up).
The design currently doesn't shift 
posture between them. The live state is 
where the highest-value behavior 
happens, and it's the state with the 
most friction.

Clarifying live state in the ﬁrst 
viewport, through motion, 
explicit labeling, or a persistent 
status badge, will increase 
watch-the-keynote 
engagement and live 
viewership duration.

creates friction for the keynote CTA
